title: Close a BLACK+DECKER LDX120C drill's clamshell over its seated motor and switch
instruction: Close up the drill housing. Lay the motor and gearbox in the open orange half, spindle through the nose, and set the trigger switch in its pocket with the trigger through its slot. Then close the other half down onto it so the two halves meet all round.
context: Team assemblers (O*NET 51-2092, 1,403,500 in their group) "work as part of a team having responsibility for assembling an entire product or component of a product"; on cordless-tool and small-appliance lines one of their stations closes the moulded clamshell over the installed motor and switch before the screws (51-2022 lists "install components, units, subassemblies, wiring, or assembly casings"). The order is set by the parts: unit and switch first, since the other half's ribs come down over both. Hard parts: (1) the 315 g unit onto two stepped ribs, spindle in a 12 mm notch; on a stop it rides 3 mm high and holds the halves open; (2) the switch's trigger through its slot; (3) the 110 g T-shaped right half carried level and set within 0.7 degrees of yaw for its hidden 3 mm tongue. Its centre of mass lies between nose and battery foot, so one grip at an end tips it: one arm alone left it 3 mm open. Closing over an unseated part: 0.
setup: Bimanual YAM station, table top the reference height; x forward from the line through the arm bases, y left of their midpoint, z up; bases at y +/-30.5 cm. Product: a BLACK+DECKER LDX120C 20 V drill/driver, its own two housing halves, motor-gearbox unit and trigger switch, taken out once (screws out, the motor's two leads disconnected from the switch) and reused every trial; nothing else. The sizes below are the simulation's model of these parts (Fidelity). The motor's lead stays soldered to the motor, unhooked from the switch, its end taped along the can. Fixed: (1) the open left half, orange ABS, open side up, parting plane 2.8 cm above the table, in a nest of three 10 mm aluminium blocks screwed to the bench 1 mm off its outline (nose, barrel top, foot end). Barrel x 23.2 to 36.3 cm, y 1.2 to 6.8 cm; handle x 25.5 to 30.1 cm, y -8.8 to 1.2 cm, ending in the battery foot, x 21.0 to 33.0 cm, y -11.8 to -8.8 cm; walls and shell 2.5 mm. Inside: two cradle ribs across the barrel at x 26.3 and 32.2 cm, each with a stepped notch whose floor is 1.0 cm up (the unit's axis then lies on the parting plane, y 4.0 cm); a low axial stop 3.5 mm beyond each end of the unit; a 12 mm notch in the nose wall for the spindle; in the handle a pocket (a 17 mm standoff and three ribs 3 mm round the switch) and a 15 mm slot in the handle's front wall for the trigger. (2) A kitting tray: two 6 mm rails along x, x 27 to 33 cm, inner edges 16 mm apart about y 26.0 cm. Loose, rigid: (3) Motor-gearbox unit, 315 g: silver 550-size can 36 x 57 mm, black gearbox 36 mm across x 45 mm, steel spindle 10 x 24 mm, rear boss 12 x 5 mm; lying on the tray rails, axis along x 2.2 cm up, spindle toward +x, can/gearbox joint at x 30.0, y 26.0 cm. (4) Trigger switch, 40 g: black body 30 (x) x 24 (y) x 22 mm with a grey 15 x 10 x 12 mm trigger out of its +x face; standing on the bench, body centre x 28.0, y -26.0 cm. (5) The right half (cover), orange ABS, 110 g: the mirror shell (barrel, handle and foot), 2.8 cm deep, ribs that come down over the unit and the switch with 1.5 mm to spare, and a 3 mm locating tongue 2 mm inside the left half's walls; open side down on the bench on its tongue, its outline x 5.5 to 20.8 cm, y -11.8 to 6.8 cm, in line with the left half. Fit: turned round, the unit or the switch does not go in; seated, the unit's top is 18 mm and the switch's 11 mm above the parting plane. The unit and switch start 26 cm left and right of the midline (one per arm); the scripted demo carries the right half with two hands (barrel nose, foot behind the handle), lets go and lifts both hands.
scoring: From the parts' poses and each gripper's pad-tip point and opening, every control step (20 Hz). 'At rest': the part's frame moved along a path under 3 mm over the last 0.5 s. 'Held': a gripper under 90% open has its pad-tip point within 15 mm of the part's surface and no farther from it than from another loose part (a tie holds both); a step whose arms cannot be read counts every part as held. A held part earns nothing and triggers no rule. 'Unit seated': not held, at rest, its can/gearbox joint on the axis within 4 mm along it (the stops allow 3.5), 2 mm across and 1.5 mm in height, its axis within 3 degrees of the barrel's with the spindle through the nose. 'Switch seated': not held, at rest, body centre within 3 mm of its seat seen from above and 1.5 mm in height (on its standoff), its body's vertical axis within 5 degrees of vertical, trigger within 8 degrees of +x (through its slot). 'Shut': the right half not held, at rest, and at each of its six outline corners (barrel 4, battery foot's far end 2) its rim within 1.5 mm of the parting plane in height and within 4 mm of the left half's matching corner seen from above. 'On the housing': the right half not held and its frame point (on the barrel's axis) inside the housing's outline seen from above. Score 0 if the right half is on the housing while a part not held has its frame inside the outline and is not seated (closed over an unseated part). Otherwise, first match: 1.0 unit and switch seated, and the halves shut; 0.7 both seated and the right half on the housing, at rest, but not shut; else 0.3 for a seated unit plus 0.2 for a seated switch (0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5), wherever the right half is. Possible scores: 0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0. The trial ends with success once 1.0 has held 1 s; else the score at the run limit, same rules. No whole-trial rule. Real trial: a 1.5 mm feeler gauge must not enter the parting line at any of the six corners; a steel rule across each corner reads the step; then lift the right half off: a photo shows the spindle in the nose notch and the trigger in its slot, a depth gauge from a straightedge on the rim reads the unit's and the switch's tops within 1.5 mm of the heights recorded at setup (18 and 11 mm in the model), a rule reads the unit's end gaps to the stops.
fidelity: Rigid boxes and cylinders, one friction. Stand-ins: the shells' curved outsides are flat boxes with 2.5 mm walls, the ribs stepped plates. Every size estimates the LDX120C's parts (the can at the common 550 size); the real trial needs none: its parts fit each other and depth references are read at setup. The tongue has 2 mm play (real about 0.5 mm) for the arms' 3 to 7 mm trail. The motor lead is not simulated (real trial: unhooked at the switch). No screws: shut goes on to screwing.
reset_notes: Lift the right half off and set it open side down in front of the nest, outline x 5.5 to 20.8 cm, in line with the left half. Lift the switch out and stand it at x 28.0, y -26.0 cm, trigger toward +x. Lift the unit out and lay it on the tray rails, spindle toward +x, can/gearbox joint at x 30.0 cm. The left half, nest and tray stay fixed. Nothing is consumed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (981 steps); one arm idle: 0.2 (left idle), 0.3 (right idle)
